source.text: በውእቱ፡ መካን፡ ርኢኩ፡ ነቅዐ፡ ጽድቅ፡ ዘኢይትኄለቍ፡ ወ*አውዳ፡ የአውዳ፡ ብዙኃ፡ አንቅዕተ፡ ጥበብ፡ ወኵሎሙ፡ ጽሙኣን፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ይሰትዩ፡ ወይትመልኡ፡ ጥበበ፡ ወማኅደሪሆሙ፡ ምስለ፡ *ጻድቃን፡ ወቅዱሳን፡ ወኅሩያን፡

current_canonical_source_text: በውእቱ፡ መካን፡ ርኢኩ፡ ነቅዐ፡ ጽድቅ፡ ዘኢይትኄለቍ፡ ወ*አውዳ፡ የአውዳ፡ ብዙኃ፡ አንቅዕተ፡ ጥበብ፡ ወኵሎሙ፡ ጽሙኣን፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ይሰትዩ፡ ወይትመልኡ፡ ጥበበ፡ ወማኅደሪሆሙ፡ ምስለ፡ *ጻድቃን፡ ወቅዱሳን፡ ወኅሩያን፡

translation.text: In that place I saw the spring of righteousness[a], which is inexhaustible, and around it were many springs of wisdom. And all the thirsty drank from them and were filled with wisdom[f][e][d][c][b], and their dwelling was with the righteous and the holy and the chosen.

footnotes.text: The Ethiopic text has a difficult expression around 'around it,' with a repeated form in the OCR witness. The sense is likely that many springs of wisdom were situated around the spring of righteousness.
Or 'fountain of righteousness' ... 'fountains of wisdom.'
'The holy' may also be rendered 'the holy ones.'
Or 'drank from them and were filled'.
Or 'around it were many springs of wisdom'.
Or 'which does not fail'.

source.text: ወበይእቲ፡ ሰዓት፡ ተጸውዐ፡ *ወልደ፡ ሰብእ፡ ዝኩ፡ በኀበ፡ እግዚአ፡ መናፈስት፡ ወስሙ፡ መቅድመ፡ ርእሰ፡ መዋዕል፡፡

current_canonical_source_text: ወበይእቲ፡ ሰዓት፡ ተጸውዐ፡ *ወልደ፡ ሰብእ፡ ዝኩ፡ በኀበ፡ እግዚአ፡ መናፈስት፡ ወስሙ፡ መቅድመ፡ ርእሰ፡ መዋዕል፡፡

translation.text: And at that hour that Son of Man was named in the presence of the Lord of Spirits[b][a], and his name was before the Head of Days.

footnotes.text: Or 'was called.' The passive verb can denote designation or naming; 'was named' is chosen because the next clause repeats 'his name.'
'Head of Days' is a literal rendering of a divine title in the Parables. It is kept rather than replaced with a smoother traditional equivalent so the imagery remains visible.

source.text: ወዘእንበለ፡ ትትፈጠር፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወታእምር፡ እንበለ፡ ይትገበሩ፡ ከዋክብተ፡ ሰማይ፡ ወስሙ፡ ተጸውዐ፡ በቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መናፈስት፡፡

current_canonical_source_text: ወዘእንበለ፡ ትትፈጠር፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወታእምር፡ እንበለ፡ ይትገበሩ፡ ከዋክብተ፡ ሰማይ፡ ወስሙ፡ ተጸውዐ፡ በቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መናፈስት፡፡

translation.text: And before the sun and the signs were created[a], before the stars of heaven were made[c][b], his name was called before the Lord of Spirits.

footnotes.text: Or 'in the presence of the Lord of Spirits.' The Ge'ez preposition can carry a courtly-presence sense as well as simple 'before.'
The verse stresses that this figure's naming precedes the creation of the sun and the heavenly stars' signs, underscoring pretemporal status.
Or "And before the sun was created, and before the signs of the heaven's stars were made, his name was called before the Lord of Spirits.".

source.text: ውእቱ፡ ይከውን፡ በትረ፡ ለጻድቃን፡ ከመ፡ ቦቱ፡ ይትመረጐዙ፡ ወኢይደቁ፡ ወውእቱ፡ *ብርሃነ፡ አሕዛብ፡ ወውእቱ፡ ይከውን፡ ተስፋ፡ ለእለ፡ የሐምሙ፡ በልቦሙ፡፡

current_canonical_source_text: ውእቱ፡ ይከውን፡ በትረ፡ ለጻድቃን፡ ከመ፡ ቦቱ፡ ይትመረጐዙ፡ ወኢይደቁ፡ ወውእቱ፡ *ብርሃነ፡ አሕዛብ፡ ወውእቱ፡ ይከውን፡ ተስፋ፡ ለእለ፡ የሐምሙ፡ በልቦሙ፡፡

translation.text: He will be a staff for the righteous[a], so that they may lean on him and not fall; and he will be the light of the nations[c][b], and he will be hope for those who are troubled in heart.

footnotes.text: Or 'a light for the nations.' The Ge'ez phrase can be rendered either way; the main text keeps the compact construct sense.
Literally, 'those who suffer/are sick in their heart.' The expression points to inward distress rather than physical illness alone.
Or 'And he will become a staff for the righteous, so that they may lean on him and not fall; and he will become the light of the nations, and he will become hope'.

source.text: ይወድቁ፡ ወይሰግዱ፡ ቅድሜሁ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ እለ፡ የኃድሩ፡ ዲበ፡ የብስ፡ ወይሴብሕዎ፡ ወይባርክዎ፡ ወይዜምሩ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መናፈስት፡፡

current_canonical_source_text: ይወድቁ፡ ወይሰግዱ፡ ቅድሜሁ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ እለ፡ የኃድሩ፡ ዲበ፡ የብስ፡ ወይሴብሕዎ፡ ወይባርክዎ፡ ወይዜምሩ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መናፈስት፡፡

translation.text: And all who dwell upon the dry land shall fall down and bow before him[a], and they shall praise and bless and sing to the Lord of Spirits.

footnotes.text: Or 'who dwell on the earth.' The Ge'ez wording is more literally 'upon the dry land.'

source.text: በእንተዝ፡ ኮነ፡ ኅሩየ፡ ወኅቡአ፡ በቅድሜሁ፡ ዘእንበለ፡ *ይትፈጠር፡ ዓለም፡ ወእስከ፡ ለዓለም።

current_canonical_source_text: በእንተዝ፡ ኮነ፡ ኅሩየ፡ ወኅቡአ፡ በቅድሜሁ፡ ዘእንበለ፡ *ይትፈጠር፡ ዓለም፡ ወእስከ፡ ለዓለም።

translation.text: For this reason[a], he was chosen and hidden before him before the world was created[c][b], and forever.

footnotes.text: Or 'in his presence.' The phrase 'before him' likely refers to God, but the translation keeps the Ge'ez relational wording.
The final phrase can also be understood more literally as 'unto eternity' or 'unto the age.'
Or 'before him before the world was created'.

source.text: ወ*ከሠተ፡ *ለቅዱሳን፡ ወለጻድቃን፡ ጥበቡ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መናፍስት፡ እስመ፡ ዐቀቡ፡ ክፍሎሙ፡ ለጻድቃን፡ እስመ፡ ጸልእዎ፡ ወመነንዎ፡ ለዝ፡ ዓለም፡ ዘዓመፃ፡ ወኵሎ፡ ምግባሮ፡ ወፍናዊሁ፡ ጸልኡ፡ *በስሙ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መናፍስት፡ እስመ፡ በስሙ፡ ዚአሁ፡ ይድኅኑ፡ ወበፈቃዱ፡ ኮነ፡ ሕይወቶሙ።

current_canonical_source_text: ወ*ከሠተ፡ *ለቅዱሳን፡ ወለጻድቃን፡ ጥበቡ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መናፍስት፡ እስመ፡ ዐቀቡ፡ ክፍሎሙ፡ ለጻድቃን፡ እስመ፡ ጸልእዎ፡ ወመነንዎ፡ ለዝ፡ ዓለም፡ ዘዓመፃ፡ ወኵሎ፡ ምግባሮ፡ ወፍናዊሁ፡ ጸልኡ፡ *በስሙ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መናፍስት፡ እስመ፡ በስሙ፡ ዚአሁ፡ ይድኅኑ፡ ወበፈቃዱ፡ ኮነ፡ ሕይወቶሙ።

translation.text: And the wisdom of the Lord of Spirits has revealed him to the holy and to the righteous[a]; for they have kept the portion of the righteous, because they hated and despised this world of unrighteousness, and they hated all its works and its ways in the name of the Lord of Spirits. For by his name they are saved[d][c][b], and by his good pleasure their life came to be.

footnotes.text: Or 'the holy ones.' The Ge'ez group term can denote consecrated people collectively.
'The portion of the righteous' may mean their allotted share, lot, or inheritance as righteous ones.
Or 'by his will their life was established.' The final clause emphasizes that the life of the righteous depends on the Lord of Spirits' willing purpose.
Or 'And wisdom was poured out for the holy and for the righteous;'.

source.text: በ*ዝንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ክኑ፡ ትሑታነ፡ ገጽ፡ ነገሥተ፡ ምድር፡ ወጽኑዓን፡ እለ፡ ይእኅዝዋ፡ ለየብስ፡ በእንተ፡ ምግባረ፡ እደዊሆሙ፡ እስመ፡ በዕለተ፡ ጻዕቆሙ፡ ወጻሕቦሙ፡ ኢይድኅኑ፡ ርእሶሙ።

current_canonical_source_text: በ*ዝንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ክኑ፡ ትሑታነ፡ ገጽ፡ ነገሥተ፡ ምድር፡ ወጽኑዓን፡ እለ፡ ይእኅዝዋ፡ ለየብስ፡ በእንተ፡ ምግባረ፡ እደዊሆሙ፡ እስመ፡ በዕለተ፡ ጻዕቆሙ፡ ወጻሕቦሙ፡ ኢይድኅኑ፡ ርእሶሙ።

translation.text: In those days the faces of the kings of the earth and the mighty who possess the dry land shall be humbled[a], because of the works of their hands; for on the day of their distress and affliction[d][c][b], they will not save themselves.

footnotes.text: Or possibly, 'their faces shall be cast down—the kings of the earth and the mighty.' The Ge'ez wording is somewhat compressed, and the relation of 'humble/lowly of face' to the following nouns is not fully certain.
'The dry land' is literal. It may simply mean the inhabited earth/land under human rule.
'Works of their hands' may carry an echo of self-made power or even idols, but the wording is left broad in the main text.
Or 'the humble of face shall be put to shame, the kings of the earth and the mighty who possess the dry land'.

source.text: ወ*ውስተ፡ እዴሆሙ፡ ለ*ኅሩያን፡ ዚአየ፡ እወድዮሙ፡ ከመ፡ ሣዕር፡ ውስተ፡ እሳት፡ ከመዝ፡ ይውዕዩ፡ እምቅድመ፡ ገጸ፡ ቅዱሳን፡ ከመ፡ ዐረር፡ ውስተ፡ ማይ፡ ይሠጠሙ፡ እምቅድመ፡ ገጸ፡ ጻድቃን፡ ወኢይትረከብ፡ ሎሙ፡ አሰር።

current_canonical_source_text: ወ*ውስተ፡ እዴሆሙ፡ ለ*ኅሩያን፡ ዚአየ፡ እወድዮሙ፡ ከመ፡ ሣዕር፡ ውስተ፡ እሳት፡ ከመዝ፡ ይውዕዩ፡ እምቅድመ፡ ገጸ፡ ቅዱሳን፡ ከመ፡ ዐረር፡ ውስተ፡ ማይ፡ ይሠጠሙ፡ እምቅድመ፡ ገጸ፡ ጻድቃን፡ ወኢይትረከብ፡ ሎሙ፡ አሰር።

translation.text: And into the hands of my chosen ones I will deliver them[a], and like straw in the fire, so they will burn before the face of the holy ones; and like lead in water, they will sink before the face of the righteous[e][d][c][b], and no trace will be found for them.

footnotes.text: The opening phrase is literally 'in the hands of the chosen ones,' which may imply being given over to their power in judgment.
Or 'like stubble in the fire.'
The final clause means that nothing remained of them—no trace or remnant could be found.
Or 'of the chosen ones I saw them'.
Or 'and they burned before the face of the holy ones like straw in the fire; and like lead in water they sank before the face of the righteous, and no trace was found'.

source.text: ወ*በ*ዕለተ፡ ጻሕበ፡ ዚአሆሙ፡ ዕረፍት፡ ትከውን፡ ዲበ፡ ምድር፡ ወበቅድሜሆሙ፡ ይወድቁ፡ ወኢይትነሥኡ፡ ወአልቦ፡ ዘይትሜጠዎሙ፡ በእዴሁ፡ ወያነሥኦሙ፡ እስመ፡ ክሕድዎ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መናፍስት፡ ወለመሢሑ፡ ወይትባረክ፡ ስሙ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መናፍስት፡

current_canonical_source_text: ወ*በ*ዕለተ፡ ጻሕበ፡ ዚአሆሙ፡ ዕረፍት፡ ትከውን፡ ዲበ፡ ምድር፡

translation.text: And on the day of their affliction[b][a], rest shall come upon the earth.

footnotes.text: Or 'affliction' or 'trouble' for 'distress.' The Ge'ez term denotes hardship or pressure; the exact nuance is not fully fixed by this short clause alone.
Or 'rest shall be upon the earth.' The verb can be rendered more literally as 'shall be' or 'shall come to be.'
